title: Data reuse, turn selection and amortizing training
subtitle: Dense-retrieval scaling · Turn-BoN · RL with notes · μP
intro: Three main readings: retrieval early stopping with limited unique data, turn-level action selection at inference, and RL with fixed notes. Briefs cover scaling, Muon, technical reports and subscribed authors. The classic is μP.

articles.title: Fit the bottom of the repeated-training curve
articles.evidence: Read Sections 3–4 and Tables 2 and 5; not reproduced

blocks.text: Supervised retrieval often repeats scarce labels, so the final checkpoint can overfit. The study fine-tunes BERT-Tiny through Base on MS MARCO, sweeping 5K–320K unique query–document pairs over 35 configurations.[1]

articles.paper: On Turn-Level Best-of-N Sampling for Scaling LLM Agents
articles.authors: Jalaj Bhandari · Dhawal Gupta · Hongli Zhan · Zhenting Wang · Varad Pimpalkhute · Zhengzhong Liu · Eric Xing · Rupesh Srivastava
articles.title: Move Best-of-N before environment execution
articles.evidence: Read method, Section 3 and Table 1; not reproduced

blocks.text: Whole-trajectory resampling selects after completion. Here a stronger off-the-shelf model ranks candidate commands at every turn, and only the chosen command reaches the environment, avoiding branch rollback.[2]

blocks.label: Method schematic: hₜ is history and S a listwise selector; no trajectory-optimality theorem [2]
Explanatory accounting: zₜ is selector output; excludes input tokens, FLOPs and wall time [2]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Terminal-Bench v2.1 uses 89 tasks with four attempts each. Better pass@1 and repeat success use more output budget; no general advantage over equal-compute trajectory sampling or with weaker selectors is established.[2]

articles.evidence: Read setup, cost model and changing-notes experiment; not reproduced

blocks.text: Notes, raw files, prompts and harness stay fixed; GRPO with LoRA changes only model weights. Training and evaluation tasks are disjoint. Controls add notes first, then RL.[3]

blocks.tex: R_\lambda(\tau)=R_{\rm task}(\tau)-\lambda C(\tau),\qquad q_*=\frac{K_{\rm train}}{c_{\rm comparator}-c_{\rm tuned}}

blocks.text: With modeled training cost of $372.57, break-even is about 3,487 queries. It depends on prices, utilization and traffic. Hex does not match the best frontier comparator, so the gains need not transfer across workspaces.[3]

classic.title: How much should one update change features as width grows?
classic.dateNote: NeurIPS 2021; first arXiv posting and version read: v1, 2022-03-07
classic.evidence: Read Sections 3–4, Table 8 and Appendix D; one-layer counting below is illustrative

recognition.label: NeurIPS 2021 · Foundational work on hyperparameter transfer (proceedings checked 2026-11-05)

classic.question: With matrix-orthogonalizing optimizers, how would coordinate checks distinguish a bad width rule from a bad attention parametrization?

blocks.text: Standard parametrization controls initialization scale without necessarily controlling feature updates. Tensor Programs’ infinite-width feature-learning analysis (2021) motivates μP; this paper turns it into small-model tuning followed by transfer.[21,22]

blocks.tex: \operatorname{Var}(W_{ij,0})\asymp n^{-1},\quad \eta_{\rm Adam,hidden}\asymp n^{-1},\quad f(x)=n^{-1}v^\top h(x),\quad \eta_{\rm Adam,readout}\asymp 1
blocks.label: Table 8 width orders: both hidden axes grow, output dimension is fixed, and v has constant initialization variance [21]
Illustrative counting: aligned normalized updates cⱼ can sum against inputs at order n; independent zero-mean cancellation is not assumed
Readout update at fixed h: explicit 1/n balances an aligned sum
One form of the coordinate check: compare average coordinate magnitudes at equal steps across widths [21]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Stable width order is an implementation diagnostic, not a guarantee of exactly invariant optimal learning rates. Transformer and ResNet experiments do not automatically cover depth changes, dataset shifts or Muon.[21]
